title: Ethical Decision Making: Kinds of Ethical Dilemmas
transcript: brought to you by global ethics solutions no matter how hard you may try to avoid them ethical dilemmas do occur however they happen you need to have a system in place to deal with them effectively most ethical dilemmas fall into one of two categories situational or not so situational dilemmas a situational dilemma is a matter of judgment moral reasoning and conscience there is an inner struggle to resist temptation and rationalization not so situational dilemmas happen despite your best efforts to prevent them they can cause you the most stress and anxiety they require a decision-making model that allows you to clarify the situation and offer constructive alternatives [Music] situational ethics is the type of ethics used to evaluate what you do in light of the situation rather than by moral absolutes for the most part situational ethics is a matter of conscience and will examples of situational dilemmas may include the misuse of company time or property peer pressure lying conflicts of interest following rules obeying laws or interpersonal conflicts these are conflicts of conscience and you can choose to do them or not the key to dealing with them is to understand why you succumb to temptation if you are like most people you usually make decisions about situational dilemmas based on what's right for you at the time of the crisis you also make ethical decisions depending on your various needs and desires the key to working through situational dilemmas is to think about the influence these have on your ethical decisions you have both physical needs and emotional needs that may influence you to make the wrong choice you should be aware of those areas in your life that open you up to temptation and fortify your character and principles to stand up and say no to unethical choices or influences [Music] no matter what the situation at hand or how ambiguous it is you have to make a choice and stick with it but understand that your decisions aren't made in a vacuum there are all kinds of variables stakeholders and mitigating factors that must be considered oftentimes it's hard to weigh all the information so it is helpful to have a process in place to help figure it out for any kind of situation your mind goes through four steps first you input and collect information from many sources second you process and study the information third you analyze outcomes usually with little time and fourth you step out and make a choice every time you make a decision you set off a chain reaction you never know how far things will go you need to control these four steps and let the factors filter through your personal moral and ethical beliefs all recognize that rules must be followed but what about all the other areas of life that are not covered by rules what do we do then this is where your moral conscience kicks in the fact is you can't always rely on outwardly imposed moral codes many areas of life do not have clear-cut rules also sometimes rules are not enforced or are universally ignored you need to develop a sense of moral justice outside of the rules that are provided although you have rules you still have the freedom of choice to obey the rules or not you are not a robot or clone but you have free will there are many times in your life where the answer to an ethical problem will be completely at your discretion now consider the gray areas where there are no rules what are some examples of accountability in your workplace that require you to have an intrinsic sense of moral justice outside the rules if you take a close look at your work environment you will find that there are more areas in your workplace that are not governed by specific rules than are this is where your character and good ethical judgment kick in it's all about knowing where your boundaries are [Music] even the most honest ethical person will eventually find himself or herself in the middle of a crisis and it's not because of anything he or she did no matter what you do to control the ethical situations in your life not so situational or critical dilemmas will come your way these kinds of workplace dilemmas may include harassment and discrimination unethical or illegal orders by supervisors organizational problems corruption the behavior of others including co-workers customers or vendors and situations out of your control remember you may not be able to control the situation but you can control your reaction to it you are not helpless you need to jump in and take control so that your ethics and values are influencing and driving the situation and not the other way around so the key to working through not so situational dilemmas is preparation and planning clear thinking courage strong character good communication and perseverance [Music] this is a global ethics solutions presentation be sure to follow us online like and share this presentation and subscribe to our channel today

title: Ethical leadership – about doing the right thing
transcript: ethical leadership is about doing the right thing ethical principles won't tell you what to do but they will guide you in good decisions it's about demonstrating through your behaviour ethical conduct being open transparent non-judgmental collaborative inclusive yet carefully balancing that with evidence sound data and information to guide good decisions in the australian ethical health alliance it aims to improve health care in australia through the articulation and affirmation of ethical principles that promote the interests of patients consumers enhance access to safe and effective health care encourage ethical collaboration in the healthcare sector and build public trust human health is all about people the australian consensus framework for ethical collaboration in the healthcare sector contains five substantive principles and ten procedural principles now one of those procedural principles is integrity and it's described as the following those engaged in collaborations are alert to competing and conflicting personal professional organisational interests and to the management of bias better health comes can be achieved through demonstration of integrity by all players in the health system now evidence-based decision making that's open and so another procedural principle is test stability these are judgments and decisions made by those engaging in collaboration that are open to independent verification and revision similar to an organization's purpose values of an organization should be sustainable through cycles periods of disruption change values are timeless the right ethical principles today should continue to apply as relevant and helpful in five to ten years an ethical organization lives and breathes its ethical framework comprised of purpose values and principles australia has learned that creating an environment to harness the good will of good people wishing to make a difference is key that leveraging and encouraging contributors to feel part of the movement in a matter that is not overbearing rather complementary to the everyday roles in life australia's learnt the importance of maintaining momentum that access to resources not expensive ones are key to ensuring that strategies and actions are progressed that the practice of good governance meeting rhythm follow-up regular communication is effective and looking to raise the profile of the ethical movement through publications in journals and so on has been effective there will always be dilemmas we should expect that as a matter of fact in our and in our everyday lives the challenge is how we respond the way in which we seek to engage the tone the approach actions speak louder than words there will always be a tension between the profit motive perhaps ranking higher among some participants in the sector and the best course of action for the patient for example financial incentives should not influence the doctor-patient relationship ethical leadership is about how do you balance these competing interests it's about demonstration role modeling mentoring education awareness and guidance and also understanding the consequences are key of unethical behavior and it's respecting that everyone has a role to play that we must take the time and effort to invest in relationships to better inform a path ahead

title: What Makes a Leader Great?
transcript: leadership is perhaps one of the most misunderstood subjects in business leadership has nothing to do with rank I know many people who sit at the highest levels of an organization who are not leaders we do as they tell us because they have authority over us but we do not trust them and we do not follow them I also know people at low levels of organizations that have no formal Authority but they've made a choice the choice to look after the person to the left of them the choice to look after the person to the right of them and we would trust them and follow them anywhere leadership is the awesome responsibility to see those around us rise you every one of us can choose to be the leader we wish we had we lead our teams and we can lead our clients when we decide that we will do everything in our power to see them rise to see them achieve their Ambitions and their dreams and this is what servant leadership means I serve your dream rather than you serve my bottom line and it's totally fine to have financial goals it's totally fine to have metrics because that becomes the proof of value that somebody wants to give you their money because they believe in you it is it is proof positive but uh uh the best leaders I know are students of leadership there's no such thing as an expert leader it doesn't exist like there's no such thing as an expert parent it doesn't exist right we are students of leadership and even the most senior leaders constantly are reading books reading articles watching talks having conversations all the time about leadership they're always in learning mode and I think for anyone who wants to be a leader uh you have to choose to be a student of the subject like anything if you want to be good at something you have to study it and the most ignored characteristic of leadership you know we talk about vision and Charisma yes these are important but I've known some wonderful leaders who don't have huge world-changing vision I've known some wonderful leaders that are quiet and sit in the corner but they all have courage the courage to advance a vision the courage to ignore the short-term ups and downs of the business the courage to take risks on people the courage to believe in people the courage to speak truth to power the courage to do the right thing and have integrity I think courage is a very undervalued characteristic of leadership
